newsitem.title: FRANCE: AOM Paris-Sydney-Nnoumea upgrade boost for freight.
newsitem.headline: AOM Paris-Sydney-Nnoumea upgrade boost for freight.

text.p: An upgrading of AOM French Airlines' passenger services to Australia and the South Pacific, will boost freight services on the route, the French airline's cargo director, Bernard Tetu, told Reuters.

"From the end of June, AOM will be adding a second weekly frequency on its Paris/Orly-Colombo-Sydney-Noumea (New Caledonia) service giving shippers the possibility of more cargo capacity and also greater flexibility in despatching goods," Tetu said.

The new frequency will leave Orly on Sundays compared to Wednesdays for the existing one and will mean shippers have the option of freight arriving in Sydney and Noumea at the end of the week or mid-week," Tetu added.

"Demand is already buoyant for cargo capacity on this service, particularly between Orly and Sydney - the only direct link from Paris and Australia - and Sydney and Noumea and the upgrade is very welcome news for freight."
AOM operates a DC10-30 aircraft on the Paris-Colombo-Sydney-Noumea service, which can carry around ten tonnes of freight on this routing.
